column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|01-25|1759|Ρόμπερτ Μπερνς|Robert Burns|Robert Burns was born in 1759 in Ayrshire, Scotland. He was a poet and is regarded as the national poet of the country. He wrote in the Scots dialect, and "Auld Lang Syne" is sung on New Year's Day. He died in 1796.

bio|08-21|2018|Στέφαν Καρλ Στέφανσον|Stefán Karl Stefánsson|Stefán Karl Stefánsson was an Icelandic actor and singer. He became known as the villain Robbie Rotten in the youth series "LazyTown". He died of cancer in 2018.

bio|08-22|1350|Φίλιππος ΣΤ΄|Philip VI|Philip VI was King of France from 1328, the first of the House of Valois. During his reign the Hundred Years' War with England began and the Black Death broke out. He died in 1350.

bio|08-22|1485|Ριχάρδος Γ΄|Richard III|Richard III was King of England from 1483. He was killed at the Battle of Bosworth in 1485 and lost the throne to Henry Tudor. He was the last king of the House of Plantagenet.

bio|08-22|1862|Κλοντ Ντεμπισί|Claude Debussy|Claude Debussy was a French composer and one of the pioneers of musical impressionism. He wrote the works "Prelude to the Afternoon of a Faun", "La Mer" and "Clair de lune". He died in 1918.

bio|08-22|1902|Λένι Ρίφενσταλ|Leni Riefenstahl|Leni Riefenstahl was a German director. She directed the propaganda films "Triumph of the Will" and "Olympia" for the Nazi regime. After the war she worked in photography. She died in 2003.
bio|08-22|1904|Τενγκ Σιαοπίνγκ|Deng Xiaoping|Deng Xiaoping was a Chinese politician. He led China from 1978 and began the economic reforms and the opening up of the country. He died in 1997.
bio|08-22|1920|Ρέι Μπράντμπερι|Ray Bradbury|Ray Bradbury was an American writer of fantasy and science fiction. He wrote "Fahrenheit 451" and "The Martian Chronicles". He died in 2012.

bio|08-22|1978|Γιόμο Κενυάτα|Jomo Kenyatta|Jomo Kenyatta was a Kenyan politician. He led the struggle for independence from Britain and became the first prime minister and president of Kenya, from 1963 to 1978.

bio|08-22|1986|Τζελάλ Μπαγιάρ|Celal Bayar|Celal Bayar was a Turkish politician. He was the third president of Turkey, from 1950 to 1960, when he was overthrown by a military coup. He lived to the age of 103.
bio|08-22|1995|Ντούα Λίπα|Dua Lipa|Dua Lipa is a British singer of Albanian origin. She became known with hits such as "New Rules" and "Don't Start Now". She has won many BRIT and Grammy awards.

bio|08-23|634|Αμπού Μπακρ|Abu Bakr|Abu Bakr was the first caliph of Islam, after the death of Muhammad. He was the father-in-law and a close associate of the prophet. He united the Arab tribes and died in 634, according to tradition.

bio|08-23|1305|Γουίλιαμ Γουάλας|William Wallace|William Wallace was a Scottish knight and leader of the Scottish resistance to the English. He defeated the English at the Battle of Stirling Bridge in 1297. He was captured and executed in London in 1305.
bio|08-23|1754|Λουδοβίκος ΙΣΤ΄|Louis XVI|Louis XVI was King of France from 1774. He was deposed during the French Revolution, and he was executed by guillotine in January 1793.

bio|08-23|1769|Ζορζ Κυβιέ|Georges Cuvier|Georges Cuvier was a French naturalist and a pioneer of comparative anatomy and palaeontology. He proved that there were species that had become extinct. He died in 1832.

bio|08-23|1806|Σαρλ Ωγκυστέν ντε Κουλόμπ|Charles-Augustin de Coulomb|Charles-Augustin de Coulomb was a French physicist. He formulated the law that describes the force between electric charges, and the unit of charge, the coulomb, bears his name.
bio|08-23|1912|Τζιν Κέλι|Gene Kelly|Gene Kelly was an American dancer, actor and director. He became known with the film "Singin' in the Rain" and "An American in Paris". He died in 1996.

bio|08-23|1933|Άντολφ Λως|Adolf Loos|Adolf Loos was an Austrian architect. In his essay "Ornament and Crime" he rejected decoration and influenced modernism. Among his works is the Looshaus in Vienna.

bio|08-23|1950|Ρόζα Οτουνμπάγιεβα|Roza Otunbayeva|Roza Otunbayeva is a politician from Kyrgyzstan. She became president of the country in 2010, after an uprising, and was the first woman president in Central Asia. She resigned in 2011.

bio|08-23|1978|Κόμπι Μπράιαντ|Kobe Bryant|Kobe Bryant was an American basketball player. He played his entire career for the Los Angeles Lakers and won five NBA championships. He was killed in 2020 in a plane crash, together with his daughter.

bio|08-24|1313|Ερρίκος Ζ΄ του Λουξεμβούργου|Henry VII of Luxembourg|Henry VII of Luxembourg was Holy Roman Emperor from 1312. He was crowned in Rome and tried to strengthen imperial authority in Italy. He died in 1313.
bio|08-24|1888|Ρούντολφ Κλαούζιους|Rudolf Clausius|Rudolf Clausius was a German physicist. He formulated the second law of thermodynamics and introduced the concept of entropy. He died in 1888.

bio|08-24|1899|Χόρχε Λουίς Μπόρχες|Jorge Luis Borges|Jorge Luis Borges was an Argentine writer. He wrote stories and essays, such as "The Aleph" and "Fictions", with themes such as time, the labyrinth and infinity. He gradually lost his sight. He died in 1986.

bio|08-24|1902|Φερνάν Μπρωντέλ|Fernand Braudel|Fernand Braudel was a French historian. In his work "The Mediterranean" he proposed studying history over long time spans, a school known as "Annales". He died in 1985.

bio|08-24|1929|Γιάσερ Αραφάτ|Yasser Arafat|Yasser Arafat was a Palestinian politician. He led the Palestine Liberation Organization and in 1994 shared the Nobel Peace Prize with Rabin and Peres. He died in 2004.

bio|08-24|1943|Σιμόν Βέιλ|Simone Weil|Simone Weil was a French philosopher and mystic. She took part in the French Resistance during the war and died in 1943 in England. She wrote "Gravity and Grace".
bio|08-24|1948|Σάουλι Νιινίστο|Sauli Niinistö|Sauli Niinistö is a Finnish politician. He was president of Finland from 2012 to 2024, when the country joined NATO.
bio|08-24|1988|Ρούπερτ Γκριντ|Rupert Grint|Rupert Grint is an English actor. He became famous as Ron Weasley in the "Harry Potter" films and has played various other roles in film and theatre.

bio|08-24|2014|Ρίτσαρντ Ατένμπορο|Richard Attenborough|Richard Attenborough was an English actor and director. He directed the film "Gandhi", which won Oscars, and appeared in "Jurassic Park". He was the brother of the naturalist David Attenborough. He died in 2014.

bio|08-25|1744|Γιόχαν Γκότφριντ Χέρντερ|Johann Gottfried Herder|Johann Gottfried Herder was a German philosopher and writer. He studied language and history and inspired the idea of the culture of peoples. He influenced Romanticism. He died in 1803.

bio|08-25|1819|Τζέιμς Βατ|James Watt|James Watt was a Scottish inventor and engineer. He improved the steam engine, which came into wide use during the Industrial Revolution. The unit of power, the watt, bears his name.

bio|08-25|1867|Μάικλ Φαραντέι|Michael Faraday|Michael Faraday was an English scientist. He discovered electromagnetic induction and formulated the laws of electrolysis. The unit of capacitance, the farad, bears his name.

bio|08-25|1880|Γκυγιώμ Απολλιναίρ|Guillaume Apollinaire|Guillaume Apollinaire was a French poet and the founder of the term "surrealism". He wrote the collections "Alcools" and "Calligrammes". He died in 1918 of flu, after a wound received in the war.

bio|08-25|1900|Φρίντριχ Νίτσε|Friedrich Nietzsche|Friedrich Nietzsche was a German philosopher and philologist. He wrote "Thus Spoke Zarathustra" and "Beyond Good and Evil". In the last years of his life he suffered from mental illness. He died in 1900.

bio|08-25|1912|Έριχ Χόνεκερ|Erich Honecker|Erich Honecker was an East German politician. He led East Germany from 1971 to 1989, when he was forced to resign shortly before the fall of the Berlin Wall. He died in 1994.
bio|08-25|1930|Σον Κόνερι|Sean Connery|Sean Connery was a Scottish actor. He became known as the first James Bond on screen and won an Oscar for "The Untouchables". He died in 2020.
bio|08-25|1947|Πάουλο Κοέλιο|Paulo Coelho|Paulo Coelho is a Brazilian writer. His novel "The Alchemist" became one of the most widely read books in the world.
bio|08-25|2012|Νηλ Άρμστρονγκ|Neil Armstrong|Neil Armstrong died in 2012. He was an American astronaut and the first person to walk on the Moon, on 20 July 1969, during the Apollo 11 mission.

bio|08-26|1723|Άντον φαν Λέβενχουκ|Antonie van Leeuwenhoek|Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was a Dutch scientist. He built microscopes and was among the first to see bacteria and microorganisms. He is considered a pioneer of microbiology.

bio|08-26|1743|Αντουάν Λωράν Λαβουαζιέ|Antoine Lavoisier|Antoine Lavoisier was a French chemist. He formulated the law of conservation of mass and gave oxygen its name. He was guillotined in 1794 during the French Revolution.
bio|08-26|1850|Λουδοβίκος Φίλιππος|Louis Philippe I|Louis Philippe was King of the French from 1830 to 1848, when he was overthrown by the February Revolution. He fled to England and died in 1850.

bio|08-26|1882|Τζέιμς Φρανκ|James Franck|James Franck was a German physicist. Together with Gustav Hertz he carried out the Franck-Hertz experiment, and in 1925 they shared the Nobel Prize in Physics. He emigrated to the United States in 1935.

bio|08-26|1910|Μητέρα Τερέζα|Mother Teresa|Mother Teresa was born in Skopje and was a Catholic nun and missionary. She founded the Missionaries of Charity in Calcutta and cared for the poor and the sick. In 1979 she was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. She died in 1997.

bio|08-26|1910|Γουίλιαμ Τζέιμς|William James|William James was an American psychologist and philosopher. He developed pragmatism and wrote "The Principles of Psychology". He was the brother of the writer Henry James. He died in 1910.

bio|08-26|1974|Τσαρλς Λίντμπεργκ|Charles Lindbergh|Charles Lindbergh was an American aviator. In 1927 he made the first non-stop direct flight from New York to Paris, in the aeroplane "Spirit of St. Louis". He died in 1974.
bio|08-26|1980|Κρις Πάιν|Chris Pine|Chris Pine is an American actor. He became known as the young James Kirk in the new "Star Trek" films and appeared in "Wonder Woman".
bio|08-26|1980|Μακόλεϊ Κάλκιν|Macaulay Culkin|Macaulay Culkin is an American actor. He became famous as a child with the film "Home Alone" and its sequel.

bio|08-27|1576|Τιτσιάνο|Titian|Titian, whose full name was Tiziano Vecellio, was an Italian painter from Venice and the leading figure of the Venetian school. He became known for his use of colour and for works such as "Venus of Urbino". He died in 1576.
bio|08-27|1635|Λόπε δε Βέγα|Lope de Vega|Lope de Vega was a Spanish playwright of the Golden Age. He wrote hundreds of plays, such as "Fuenteovejuna" and "The Maid of Olmedo". He died in 1635.

bio|08-27|1770|Γκέοργκ Βίλχελμ Φρίντριχ Χέγκελ|Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel|Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel was a German philosopher of idealism. He wrote the "Phenomenology of Spirit" and developed the dialectical method, which had a great influence on Marx. He died in 1831.

bio|08-27|1908|Λίντον Τζόνσον|Lyndon B. Johnson|Lyndon B. Johnson was the 36th president of the United States. He took office after the assassination of Kennedy in 1963 and promoted the programmes of the "Great Society". His involvement in the Vietnam War marked his term. He died in 1973.

bio|08-27|1941|Σεζάρια Έβορα|Cesária Évora|Cesária Évora was a singer from Cape Verde, known as "the barefoot diva". She made morna music famous and became known internationally in the 1990s. She died in 2011.

bio|08-27|1965|Λε Κορμπυζιέ|Le Corbusier|Le Corbusier was a Swiss-French architect and theorist, a pioneer of modernism. He designed the Villa Savoye and the Unité d'Habitation in Marseille. He died in 1965 while swimming.

bio|08-27|1975|Χαϊλέ Σελασιέ Α΄|Haile Selassie I|Haile Selassie I was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930. He was deposed in 1974 by a military coup and died in 1975 while in detention. For the Rastafari he was a symbol of divine presence.

bio|08-27|1983|Τζαμάλα|Jamala|Jamala is a Ukrainian singer of Crimean Tatar origin. She won the Eurovision Song Contest in 2016 with the song "1944", which refers to the deportation of the Crimean Tatars.

bio|08-27|1986|Σεμπάστιαν Κουρτς|Sebastian Kurz|Sebastian Kurz is an Austrian politician. He became Chancellor of Austria in 2017, at the age of 31, one of the youngest leaders in the world, and he resigned in 2021.

bio|08-28|430|Αυγουστίνος|Augustine of Hippo|Augustine was bishop of Hippo in North Africa and an important theologian of the West. He wrote the "Confessions" and "The City of God". He died in 430, while the Vandals were besieging his city.
bio|08-28|1645|Ούγκο Γκρότιους|Hugo Grotius|Hugo Grotius was a Dutch lawyer and philosopher. His work "On the Law of War and Peace" is considered a foundation of international law. He died in 1645.

bio|08-28|1749|Γιόχαν Βόλφγκανγκ φον Γκαίτε|Johann Wolfgang von Goethe|Johann Wolfgang von Goethe was a German poet and writer. He wrote "Faust" and "The Sorrows of Young Werther". He also engaged with science. He died in 1832.

bio|08-28|1942|Ζοζέ Εντουάρντο ντος Σάντος|José Eduardo dos Santos|José Eduardo dos Santos was president of Angola from 1979 to 2017. During his time the country went through a civil war and later reconstruction. He died in 2025.
bio|08-28|1957|Ίβο Γιοσίποβιτς|Ivo Josipović|Ivo Josipović is a Croatian politician, lawyer and composer. He was president of Croatia from 2010 to 2015.
bio|08-28|1965|Σανάια Τουέιν|Shania Twain|Shania Twain is a Canadian country and pop singer. The album "Come On Over" was one of the best-selling albums in the history of the genre.

bio|08-28|1969|Τζακ Μπλακ|Jack Black|Jack Black is an American actor, singer and guitarist. He is a member of the comedy rock duo Tenacious D and has played in films such as "School of Rock" and "Kung Fu Panda".
bio|08-28|1987|Τζον Χιούστον|John Huston|John Huston was an American director. He directed "The Maltese Falcon", "The Treasure of the Sierra Madre" and "The African Queen". He died in 1987.
bio|08-28|1995|Μίχαελ Έντε|Michael Ende|Michael Ende was a German writer of children's and young adult literature. He wrote "The Neverending Story" and "Momo". He died in 1995.

bio|08-29|1632|Τζων Λοκ|John Locke|John Locke was an English philosopher and physician. He is regarded as the father of liberalism, and he wrote "An Essay Concerning Human Understanding" and "Two Treatises of Government". He died in 1704.

bio|08-29|1780|Ζαν Ωγκύστ Ντομινίκ Ενγκρ|Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres|Jean-Auguste-Dominique Ingres was a French neoclassical painter. He painted "The Grande Odalisque" and "The Bather". He died in 1867.

bio|08-29|1862|Μωρίς Μαίτερλινκ|Maurice Maeterlinck|Maurice Maeterlinck was a Belgian poet and playwright. He wrote the play "The Blue Bird" and "Pelléas and Mélisande". In 1911 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1949.
bio|08-29|1904|Μουράτ Ε΄|Murad V|Murad V was an Ottoman sultan for about three months in 1876. He was deposed because of mental illness and lived under confinement until his death in 1904.

bio|08-29|1936|Τζον Μακέιν|John McCain|John McCain was an American politician and military officer. He was a senator for Arizona and the Republican candidate for the presidency in 2008. He was a prisoner of war in Vietnam. He died in 2018.

bio|08-29|1958|Μάικλ Τζάκσον|Michael Jackson|Michael Jackson was born in 1958 in Gary, Indiana. He was a singer and dancer and is called "the King of Pop". The album "Thriller" is among the best-selling albums of all time. He died in 2009.
bio|08-29|1982|Ίνγκριντ Μπέργκμαν|Ingrid Bergman|Ingrid Bergman was a Swedish actress. She starred in the films "Casablanca" and "Vertigo" and won three Oscars. She died in 1982, on her birthday.
bio|08-29|1987|Λι Μάρβιν|Lee Marvin|Lee Marvin was an American actor. He played tough characters in films such as "The Dirty Dozen" and won an Oscar for "Cat Ballou". He died in 1987.

bio|08-29|2016|Τζιν Γουάιλντερ|Gene Wilder|Gene Wilder was an American actor and comedian. He appeared in the films "The Producers", "Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory" and "Young Frankenstein". He died in 2016.
bio|08-30|1797|Μαίρη Σέλεϊ|Mary Shelley|Mary Shelley was an English writer. She wrote the novel "Frankenstein" when she was only 18. She was the wife of the poet Percy Shelley. She died in 1851.

bio|08-30|1852|Ιάκωβος Ερρίκος βαν'τ Χοφ|Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff|Jacobus Henricus van 't Hoff was a Dutch chemist. He contributed to chemical kinetics and stereochemistry and in 1901 became the first person to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1911.

bio|08-30|1871|Έρνεστ Ράδερφορντ|Ernest Rutherford|Ernest Rutherford was born in New Zealand. He was a physicist and is regarded as the "father of nuclear physics". He discovered the nucleus of the atom and in 1908 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1937.
bio|08-30|1940|Τζόζεφ Τζον Τόμσον|J. J. Thomson|Joseph John Thomson was an English physicist. He discovered the electron in 1897 and in 1906 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics. He died in 1940.

bio|08-30|1954|Αλεξάντερ Λουκασένκο|Alexander Lukashenko|Alexander Lukashenko is a Belarusian politician. He has been president of Belarus since 1994, with a government that is widely criticised internationally for suppressing the opposition.
bio|08-30|1972|Κάμερον Ντίαζ|Cameron Diaz|Cameron Diaz is an American actress. She became known with the film "The Mask" and played in "There's Something About Mary" and "Charlie's Angels".

bio|08-30|2006|Ναγκίμπ Μαχφούζ|Naguib Mahfouz|Naguib Mahfouz was an Egyptian writer. He wrote "The Cairo Trilogy" and in 1988 became the first Arabic-language writer to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2006.

bio|08-30|2013|Σέιμους Χίνι|Seamus Heaney|Seamus Heaney was an Irish poet. He wrote poetry about rural life and the history of Northern Ireland, and in 1995 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 2013.

bio|08-30|2022|Μιχαήλ Γκορμπατσόφ|Mikhail Gorbachev|Mikhail Gorbachev was the last leader of the Soviet Union. As General Secretary from 1985 he introduced "glasnost" and "perestroika", and in 1990 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize. He died in 2022.

bio|08-31|12|Γάιος Καλιγούλας|Caligula|Caligula, whose real name was Gaius Caesar, was a Roman emperor from 37 to 41. His reign is remembered for arbitrariness and violence. He was assassinated in 41 by officers of his guard.

bio|08-31|161|Κόμμοδος|Commodus|Commodus was a Roman emperor from 180 to 192, the son of Marcus Aurelius. He was authoritarian and appeared as a gladiator. He was murdered in 192, and his death brought civil conflict.
bio|08-31|1867|Σαρλ Μπωντλαίρ|Charles Baudelaire|Charles Baudelaire was a French poet. His collection "The Flowers of Evil" marked modern poetry and symbolism. He died in 1867 in Paris.

bio|08-31|1870|Μαρία Μοντεσσόρι|Maria Montessori|Maria Montessori was an Italian doctor and educator. She developed the Montessori educational method, with an emphasis on the child's independent learning. She died in 1952.

bio|08-31|1880|Βιλελμίνη|Wilhelmina|Wilhelmina was Queen of the Netherlands from 1890 to 1948. In the Second World War she fled to London and supported the resistance. She abdicated in favour of her daughter Juliana.

bio|08-31|1941|Μαρίνα Τσβετάγεβα|Marina Tsvetaeva|Marina Tsvetaeva was a Russian poet. She lived for years in exile, and when she returned to the Soviet Union she was marginalised. She took her own life in 1941.
bio|08-31|1949|Ρίτσαρντ Γκιρ|Richard Gere|Richard Gere is an American actor. He became known with the films "An Officer and a Gentleman", "Pretty Woman" and "Chicago". He is involved with Buddhism.
bio|08-31|1973|Τζον Φορντ|John Ford|John Ford was an American director. He directed mainly westerns, such as "Stagecoach" and "The Searchers", and won four Oscars for Best Director. He died in 1973.

bio|08-31|1997|Νταϊάνα|Diana, Princess of Wales|Diana, Princess of Wales, was killed on 31 August 1997 in a car accident in Paris, at the age of 36. She was the former wife of Prince Charles and was greatly loved for her charity work.

bio|09-01|1557|Ζακ Καρτιέ|Jacques Cartier|Jacques Cartier was a French explorer. He explored the Saint Lawrence River in Canada and contributed to the name of the country. His date of death, 1 September 1557, is the one usually given.

bio|09-01|1715|Λουδοβίκος ΙΔ΄|Louis XIV|Louis XIV, the "Sun King", reigned over France for 72 years, from 1643 to 1715, the longest reign in European history. He built Versailles and fought many wars.
bio|09-01|1875|Έντγκαρ Ράις Μπάροουζ|Edgar Rice Burroughs|Edgar Rice Burroughs was an American writer. He created "Tarzan" in 1912 and also wrote science fiction novels about Mars. He died in 1950.
bio|09-01|1946|Ρο Μού-χιον|Roh Moo-hyun|Roh Moo-hyun was a South Korean politician and human rights lawyer. He was president of South Korea from 2003 to 2008. He took his own life in 2009.

bio|09-01|1954|Φίλιπ Βουγιάνοβιτς|Filip Vujanović|Filip Vujanović is a Montenegrin politician. He served as prime minister and as president, and he led the country to independence from Serbia in 2006.

bio|09-01|1957|Γκλόρια Εστέφαν|Gloria Estefan|Gloria Estefan is a Cuban-American singer and songwriter. Together with the group Miami Sound Machine she recorded hits such as "Conga" and "Rhythm Is Gonna Get You".
bio|09-01|1962|Ρουντ Γκούλιτ|Ruud Gullit|Ruud Gullit is a former Dutch footballer. He played for Milan and for the Netherlands national team, which won Euro 1988. He also became a coach.
bio|09-01|1970|Φρανσουά Μωριάκ|François Mauriac|François Mauriac was a French writer. He wrote "Thérèse Desqueyroux" and in 1952 was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1970.

bio|09-01|1981|Άλμπερτ Σπέερ|Albert Speer|Albert Speer was a German architect. He was Hitler's Minister of Armaments and was sentenced at the Nuremberg trial to 20 years' imprisonment. He later wrote memoirs. He died in 1981.

bio|09-02|406|Αττίλας|Attila|Attila was king of the Huns from 434 to 453. He invaded the Balkans and France and threatened Byzantium and Rome. The date and year of his birth are not known for certain.

bio|09-02|1877|Φρέντερικ Σόντυ|Frederick Soddy|Frederick Soddy was an English chemist. He studied radioactivity and introduced the concept of isotopes. In 1921 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1956.

bio|09-02|1894|Γιόζεφ Ροτ|Joseph Roth|Joseph Roth was an Austrian writer of Jewish origin. He wrote the novel "The Radetzky March" about the fall of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. He died in 1939 in Paris.

bio|09-02|1937|Πιερ ντε Κουμπερτέν|Pierre de Coubertin|Pierre de Coubertin was a French educator and the founder of the modern International Olympic Committee. He inspired the organisation of the first modern Olympic Games, in 1896 in Athens. He died in 1937.
bio|09-02|1964|Κιάνου Ριβς|Keanu Reeves|Keanu Reeves is a Canadian actor. He became known with the "Matrix" trilogy and with the films "Speed" and "John Wick".

bio|09-02|1966|Σάλμα Χάγιεκ|Salma Hayek|Salma Hayek is a Mexican actress and producer. She starred in the film "Frida", for which she was nominated for an Oscar, and she also played in other films in Hollywood.
bio|09-02|1969|Χο Τσι Μιν|Ho Chi Minh|Ho Chi Minh was a Vietnamese revolutionary and politician. He led the struggle for independence from France and was president of North Vietnam. He died in 1969.
bio|09-02|1973|Τζ. Ρ. Ρ. Τόλκιν|J. R. R. Tolkien|J. R. R. Tolkien was a British writer and professor of philology. He wrote "The Hobbit" and "The Lord of the Rings". He died in 1973.
bio|09-02|2016|Ισλάμ Καρίμοφ|Islam Karimov|Islam Karimov was the first president of Uzbekistan after independence in 1991. He governed in an authoritarian manner until his death in 2016.
